subject: Data collection map and retention for inference outputs — follow-up
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Emily Brooks <emily.brooks@medsys.io>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data collection map and retention for inference outputs — follow-up

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really useful to understand MedSys's integration pattern and regulatory constraints. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups we promised to document: 

What we heard (short):
- You will send user-provided clinical text to Redwood for inference (summaries, triage suggestions).
- MedSys must avoid persistent storage of PHI-containing prompts unless encrypted and customer-controlled.
- Audit requirements: row-level access logs retained for an audit window (you mentioned 12–18 months).
- Preferred residency: EU only for this project (data-at-rest and audit logs).

Requested clarifications / questions for you:
1) For prompts that may contain PHI, is a 24-hour ephemeral retention window (app-driven TTL) acceptable, or do you require no server-side persistence at all?
2) Do you need plaintext prompt/response content available in audit logs, or are cryptographic hashes + metadata (timestamp, model id, route) sufficient?
3) Are there field-level redaction requirements (e.g., SSNs, MRNs) that we need to automate server-side, or will MedSys perform client-side redaction before calls?

What we can provide today (short):
- Configurable retention profiles: Ephemeral (no persistent prompt storage beyond N hours), Audit-only (store hashed prompt + metadata), Full-storage (customer-managed keys + residency controls).
- KMS/HSM integrations and key-wrapping so customer controls encryption keys for any stored content.
- EU Dedicated option (data-at-rest + logs in region) and on-prem private deploy for air-gapped needs.
- Audit logs (append-only) by default retained 13 months; configurable longer retention for enterprise contracts.

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft data collection matrix and a stub SOC 2 evidence export to help your security team triage.

Next suggested steps:
- Confirm whether 24-hour ephemeral retention is acceptable for prompt storage (yes/no).
- Confirm whether audit logs need plaintext or hashed prompt snapshots.
- If yes to longer log retention or on-prem, we’ll scope Dedicated POC and send provisioning checklist.

Happy to jump back on a call with your Security/Legal — proposed window next Wed/Thu.

Best,
Marcus

From: Emily Brooks <emily.brooks@medsys.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medsys.io
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Data collection map and retention for inference outputs — follow-up

Marcus,

Thanks for the clear recap — helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Correct, this is clinical text and will frequently contain PHI. Our starting expectation is that PHI is not persisted in plaintext on vendor systems. A 24-hour ephemeral window would be acceptable for session troubleshooting, but we need an option that guarantees automatic purge after that window.
- For audit purposes, we need access logs that tie actions to a user/service account and retain them for 13 months. We would prefer prompt content to be hashed (SHA-256 or equivalent) in logs rather than stored plaintext.
- Field-level redaction: we will do primary redaction client-side for obvious identifiers, but we also need the vendor to support server-side redaction/transformations for edge cases. Can Redwood support a server-side pipeline that masks MRNs/SSNs with configurable regexes?

A couple of asks before Security & Legal will sign off: 
1) A short one-page statement from Redwood confirming options for ephemeral versus persistent storage and confirmation of EU residency options.
2) A sample audit log schema (column list) showing which fields are included and which are hashed/obfuscated.

We’ll loop our security contact on the thread (cc’d). Can you get those two artifacts over by EOD Monday? We’re trying to keep the procurement timeline tight.

Thanks,
Emily Brooks
Head of Integrations | MedSys
emily.brooks@medsys.io
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Emily Brooks <emily.brooks@medsys.io>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data collection map and retention for inference outputs — follow-up

Emily — appreciate the specificity. See responses inline below (quoted for clarity).

> Our starting expectation is that PHI is not persisted in plaintext on vendor systems. A 24-hour ephemeral window would be acceptable for session troubleshooting, but we need an option that guarantees automatic purge after that window.

Answer: Redwood supports an Ephemeral retention profile that automatically purges prompt + response payloads after a configurable TTL. We can set the default TTL to 24 hours for the MedSys account; purge is asynchronous but guaranteed within the window. For additional assurance we offer:
- Customer-managed encryption keys (KMS/HSM) so that any stored artifacts are unreadable without your keys.
- Option for zero-persistence mode for Hosted (no long-term storage of prompt/response content) — recommended for highest assurance to run in Dedicated or Private for regulated workloads.

> For audit purposes, we need access logs that tie actions to a user/service account and retain them for 13 months. We would prefer prompt content to be hashed (SHA-256 or equivalent) in logs rather than stored plaintext.

Answer: We provide append-only audit logs that include: timestamp, request id, model id, route, requester identity, and prompt hash (SHA-256). The default retention for audit logs in our enterprise settings is 13 months; we can store those logs in an EU region. Plaintext prompt export into the audit log is an opt-in enterprise feature and will require customer-managed keys.

> Can Redwood support a server-side pipeline that masks MRNs/SSNs with configurable regexes?

Answer: Yes — we offer two patterns:
1) Client-side SDK redaction: recommended first line (fastest, simplest).
2) Server-side pre-processing rules: Redwood can run a configurable pre-processing step that applies regex-based redaction or replace-with-token transforms. We’ll propose a small rule set to start (MRN, SSN, DOB). Rules are stored per-customer and can be updated via the Console.

Attachments & artifacts: I’ve attached the one-page storage statement and a sample audit-log-schema (spreadsheet). Also included is an EU Dedicated provisioning checklist (for the POC). Links below: HubSpot deal (MS-4512) and a shared Drive folder with the artifacts.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll upload the one-pager and audit schema to your Drive by EOD Monday.
- If that looks good, we can schedule a short (30m) Security sync next Tue to walk through the rule set and provisioning steps.
- Monica (cc’d) will scope Dedicated POC cost and provisioning timeline.

Can you confirm the 24-hour TTL acceptance and whether the hashed-prompt + metadata log model is sufficient for audit? Once we have that confirmed we’ll prepare the SOW addendum.

Best,
Marcus
